name: bm25-ranking
title: bm25-ranking: score documents against all query terms, rare terms weighted more
interface:
Module `lib/rank.mjs`.

```stub
export function rank(reader: object, queryTerms: string[], limit: number): string[];
```

- `reader` is any object implementing the inverted-index reader interface
  (docCount, avgDocLen, docId(i), docLen(i), postings(term)); rank must not touch
  the filesystem itself, so it can be exercised against a hand-built reader.
- Scores with BM25 (idf = ln(1 + (N - df + 0.5) / (df + 0.5))), so a rare term
  contributes more than a common one, with saturating term frequency and document
  length normalisation, and a title occurrence weighted above a body occurrence.
- Ranks by how well a document matches ALL query terms: covering more of the query's
  known terms dominates scoring higher on a subset of them.
- Returns at most `limit` document ids, best first, only documents whose score is
  above zero, each id at most once. Ties break deterministically by ascending id.
- Query terms absent from the index contribute nothing and do not disqualify anyone;
  an empty term list returns [].
nl_description: The relevance half of the search engine: the scoring function that decides which ten documents come back and in what order, judged as mean P@10 over hidden labelled queries. It is a pure function over a reader interface — no files, no CLI — so its behaviour (rare terms outrank common ones, full query coverage outranks partial, titles outrank bodies, shorter documents outrank padded ones) is tested directly instead of inferred from end-to-end output.
